done: Made local branch fix-int at 97b4ecb5 (rel-base). Merged the five fix branches in order, one merge commit each: fix-terminal e6dfab52 -> e19b0eca, fix-site ccdfb177 -> 8a737ed3, fix-auth 419ee368 -> e6123c07, fix-plans 27961340 -> 9d8b55cf, fix-records 905bad65 -> fad74ab1. Every merge message ends with the two attribution lines.

Conflicts resolved so both tracks' intent is kept. (1) apps/edge-bff/tests/conftest.py applies the migrations in number order: 010-012, 020-023, 030, 040, 050. (2) config.py keeps the site track's email-log and EDGE_SITE checks and uses the auth track's is_verifier. (3) main.py: the sign-in clears its throttle count only after the session is made (auth, R2-9), and the old session is read under the __Host- name (plans); both tracks' imports are kept. (4) errors.py: every refusal message comes from the plans track's words(), which falls back to message_of(code, status, details), so the auth track's SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT still states its own wait. UnexpectedErrors and failure_class are kept. (5) security.py keeps both the verifier costs and the __Host- cookie names. (6) principal.py refresh_names reads both the capability kind (live_view flags) and the plan names (PLAN_EXPIRED). (7) backtest.py imports BETA and words. (8) edge-labels.js keeps USER_CHANGED and the auth track's sign-in wait wording. (9) test_c2_e2e_people.py takes the union of both tracks' imports. (10) auth_flows.py takes the union of imports, hooks included. (11) pending/README.md keeps test_cp0_runner_key.py and drops the test_r2_trace_beta_live.py row, since that test moved back to apps/edge-bff/tests.

Fixed a bug where two tracks meet: the auth track's register route (R1-11) read the held registration cookie under its plain name. On https the plans track gives that cookie the __Host- name (R2-22), so the read now uses registration_cookie (apps/edge-bff/app/auth_flows.py, register route).

Two tracks had separate purge mechanisms. The auth track's outbox purge (R2-24) is now the fourth entry of the site track's store.PURGES (R2-33), after the pending purge, so the hourly housekeeping runs it in batches, each in its own transaction, with the try-lock. To support this, edge_bff.purge_email_outbox now takes max_rows (NULL or anything above 10 000 means 10 000). This changed the unapplied migration database/migrations/20261119_012_edge_bff_email_outbox_purge.sql (function signature, comment, grants, verify block, rollback), store.ready (it reads purge_email_outbox(integer)), mailer.purge_outbox(c, limit) and two lines of the edge-bff README.

Fixed a failure the site track did not see because it did not run terminal-api's tests. The planned edge-bff-live block in .railway/railway.ts was written as a commented service("edge-bff-live", {...}) call. apps/terminal-api/tests/test_api.py::test_railway_healthcheck_probes_the_port_the_app_listens_on reads every service call in the file, comments included, so it treated the block as a declared service. The fix is in railway.ts, not the test: the block keeps every setting, and only the call's opening and closing lines are replaced by a line naming the service (commit 9a22ee75).

Changed one test, with a stated reason: apps/edge-bff/tests/test_beta_live_site.py::test_a_purge_another_instance_runs_is_skipped_and_every_purge_is_bounded. It pinned PURGES to the site track's three purges, and the merged design has four, as the site track's own notes foresaw. The test is stronger now: it also holds the outbox purge to the batch bound (7 rows in batches of 3 give 3, 3, 1, 0). Commit 2fddd030.

SCREENER_ONBOARDING.md: the pointers into the merged edge-bff main.py and screener.py are moved to the right lines: TERMINAL_ROUTES at main.py:72, Screeners at screener.py:681, screeners.routes at main.py:767, /screener at 522, the screener-app routes at 620-632, SCREENER_CSP at 108-111 (commit c6e87ee2).

Every test from the re-check's findings passes on HEAD: the edge-bff test_c2_*, test_c_p*, test_cdb_*, test_cp0_*, test_cp1a_* and test_r2_* files, the Terminal c_p1s_* vitests, and the workers' c-p3b-recheck tests. Tests the builders changed with a stated reason stay as they changed them.

Postgres cluster int1 (port 55571) was used for every Postgres suite and is now stopped. Nothing was pushed or deployed, Railway was not called and no remote database was touched. `git diff --check 97b4ecb5 HEAD` is clean.

Decision 1 of the fix round (the free plan and the guest see and search the whole ticker list; any ticker other than their own opens a sign-in or upgrade box) is not built. On HEAD, fix-terminal's R2-32 serves the free plan reference lists that hold BBCA only. Its test apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c2_e2e_people.py::test_the_free_plans_terminal_opens_on_bbca_with_nothing_remembered asserts that BBRI and TLKM are not on the page. That expectation contradicts decision 1 and must change when the decision is built (3c/3e); I left it as is because building it is outside integration.

Decision 4 (R1-2: keep MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY on orc-test-runner, 'leave as is') makes verification/edge_multiuser/access_tiers/pending/test_cp0_runner_key.py and its README row obsolete: they wait for the variable to be deleted. The README row and CONTRACT 7 ('R1-2 open') should be rewritten to the decision, including the privacy text stating that agents' jobs on the runner may read conversations. I left the pending test unchanged, since it is outside every suite.

Not run, as allowed: the Terminal look check (verification/terminal_api/terminal_look/look_check11.mjs). There is no look change in the integration; the only Terminal source change is the R1-20 key removal in src/app/assets.ts. One attempt without its data folder argument timed out waiting for #indMenu; that was not investigated. Also not run: the Screener smoke scripts and the real-data look-ahead check.

decisions_needed.topic: Seed mark after a password rehash (auth R2-29 meets site R2-2)
decisions_needed.context: User #1 is the admin account that exists from the start. While the switch is off, the start-up copies the admin's password from the setting EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER into the account, but only while the account still holds the copy the start-up itself wrote. It tells by a fingerprint of that copy (identities.seed_verifier_sha256, site track). Separately, the auth track replaces an old-format password hash with a new one at the next switch-on sign-in; the password stays the same. After that replacement the stored hash no longer matches the fingerprint, so every later beta start treats the account as having set its own password and stops copying from EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER. If the admin later changes EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER on the beta, the live site keeps the old password. No test covers this case, and it only matters once the switch is on (the live site).
decisions_needed.options: A: keep as merged (after the first switch-on sign-in, the account counts as having its own password; changing the admin password then means a change or reset on live). B: when the rehash replaces a hash that is still the start-up's copy, update the fingerprint too, so later changes to EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER keep reaching the account; the start-up would then write the old-format hash back and the next sign-in would rehash it again.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A, since it is safe and matches the R2-2 rule ('never overwritten once the identity differs from the seed's copy'); record it in CONTRACT 1 next to the seed mark.
